desc:
Reduce the Fibonacci sequence modulo m: it begins 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, ... and each term is the sum of the two before it, taken modulo m. Each term depends only on the previous two, so the sequence eventually returns to the pair 0, 1.

The Pisano period π(m) is the smallest p ≥ 1 such that Fp is congruent to 0 and Fp+1 is congruent to 1 modulo m. Return π(m).

m = 2  -> 3   (0 1 1 0 1 1 ...)
m = 3  -> 8
m = 10 -> 60
hints: Simulate the sequence modulo m, keeping only the last two terms, and stop when the pair (0, 1) appears again.
Start from the pair (F<sub>0</sub>, F<sub>1</sub>) = (0, 1) and count the steps until that pair comes back.
The period never exceeds 6m, so a loop of at most 6m steps always finishes. For m up to 20,000 that is fast.
editorial: Keep the current pair (a, b) = (Fk mod m, Fk+1 mod m), starting at (0, 1 mod m). Each step replaces the pair by (b, (a + b) mod m). The pair is a deterministic function of its predecessor and it starts at (0, 1), so the first step at which it returns to (0, 1) is exactly the period.

The period is known to be at most 6m, so the loop runs at most 120,000 steps for m = 20,000. Smaller moduli often have much shorter periods, as with pi(2) = 3, but simulation handles every case without special treatment.
